content.value_statement: Teams can misuse Diasporic Intelligence by removing source credit, consent, provenance, or revocation. This skill gives clear definitions, attribution language, boundary tests, and implementation checks.
actual_capabilities: Defines Diasporic Intelligence as Afrotemporalism in Action with concise and technical versions.
Provides attribution language for public writing, product copy, citations, and repository references.
Reviews usage against consent, provenance, revocation, lineage, and accountability requirements.
Distinguishes aligned dialogic AI from voice cloning, ancestor impersonation, and cultural data extraction.
Supplies benchmark prompts for grant, product, architecture, essay, and misuse review scenarios.
Maps implementation requirements to consent states, provenance metadata, audit logs, and role boundaries.
limitations: It is a normative documentation skill, not a legal enforcement mechanism.
It does not grant certification, endorsement, data access, or private implementation rights.
It cannot verify real consent records unless the user provides evidence.
It does not replace legal, clinical, pastoral, or community governance review.

use_cases.title: Review Product Language
use_cases.description: Check whether a product description uses Diasporic Intelligence without removing consent, provenance, revocation, or source authority.

use_cases.title: Prepare Public Attribution
use_cases.description: Draft concise credit language for essays, grant proposals, websites, or documentation that mention the framework.

use_cases.title: Assess Technical Alignment
use_cases.description: Evaluate whether an AI architecture includes consent states, provenance metadata, audit logs, revocation paths, and role boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the Term
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a clear definition.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain Diasporic Intelligence in plain language. Include the source credit and the role of consent, provenance, and revocation.

prompt_templates.title: Shorten With Attribution
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite this paragraph about Diasporic Intelligence for a public website. Keep the attribution and avoid generic cultural AI language: [paste text]

prompt_templates.title: Review a Proposed Use
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of a product, grant, or museum proposal.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this proposed use of Diasporic Intelligence. Classify it as aligned, borderline, or not aligned, and explain needed changes: [paste proposal]

prompt_templates.title: Design Governance Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a high-level governance model for a Diasporic Intelligence implementation. Include consent states, provenance, revocation, audit logs, role boundaries, and limits.

output_examples.input: Can our elder voice-cloning product call itself Diasporic Intelligence?
output_examples.output: Not as described. The framework requires consent, provenance, revocation, source authority, and non-impersonation boundaries. Redesign it as a governed oral-history support tool before using the term.

output_examples.input: Make this attribution shorter for a grant paragraph.
output_examples.output: Diasporic Intelligence, as defined by Minista Jazz / Jasmaine Cook-Kendrick, carries lineage wisdom through consent-governed voice, memory, and dialogic AI.

output_examples.input: Does our architecture qualify if consent is only captured at signup?
output_examples.output: No. Signup consent alone is not enough. The design needs event-level consent, traceable provenance, future-facing revocation, documented limits, and accountable stewardship.

best_practices: Credit Rev. Jasmaine Acelia Cook-Kendrick / Minista Jazz close to first use.
Start reviews with consent, provenance, revocation, role boundaries, and community accountability.
Document downstream limits in plain language when full revocation cannot be guaranteed.
anti_patterns: Calling generic multicultural AI or voice cloning Diasporic Intelligence without governance controls.
Removing the source name to make copy shorter or more commercial.
Presenting a chatbot as an ancestor, deity, clinician, pastor, or legal authority.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps users explain, cite, review, and implement Diasporic Intelligence while keeping source credit and governance requirements attached.

faq.question: Who is credited as the source?
faq.answer: The skill credits Rev. Jasmaine Acelia Cook-Kendrick, also known as Minista Jazz, through Much Different World in 2026.

faq.question: Is this a general Afrofuturism explainer?
faq.answer: No. It distinguishes Diasporic Intelligence from Afrofuturism and focuses on a specific consent-governed framework.

faq.question: Can this approve a legal use of the term?
faq.answer: No. It can assess framework alignment, but it is not legal advice or an enforcement mechanism.

faq.question: What makes an implementation aligned?
faq.answer: An aligned implementation includes explicit consent states, traceable provenance, revocation or correction paths, role boundaries, and documented limits.

faq.question: Does attribution alone make a project compliant?
faq.answer: No. Attribution is required, but the framework also requires consent, provenance, revocation, lineage boundaries, and community accountability.
